questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Two sides of a job market
questions.learningObjective: Identify which party a vacancy represents
questions.stem: Item 0001 asks which side of the job market a posted vacancy represents in the engineer's brief.

options.text: It represents the employer seeking to fill a position
It represents the worker seeking new employment
options.misconception: confuses the hiring side with the seeking side

options.text: It represents a government regulator of wages
It represents a training provider for skills
options.misconception: mistakes a vacancy for a course offer

questions.explanation: A vacancy is posted by the employer to attract candidates. The other options mistake it for a worker, regulator, or trainer.
questions.hint: A vacancy is posted by the hiring side.

provenance.author: bank-team-chinese
provenance.attestation: authored from first principles; no protected content used

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: What a vacancy notice selects for attention
questions.learningObjective: Explain why a notice highlights certain traits
questions.stem: Item 0002 asks why a vacancy notice in the brief highlights required skills over other details.

answer.exemplar: A vacancy notice highlights required skills because it filters applicants early and saves review time for the hiring team handling the engineer's brief.

questions.explanation: Notices foreground skills to filter candidates quickly. Details like culture come later in the process.
questions.hint: Notices filter applicants by stated skills.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.learningObjective: Sequence the steps of a job search

stimulus.body: A candidate in the engineer's brief reads a vacancy, checks the requirements, prepares a packet, and submits it before the deadline.

questions.stem: Item 0003 asks which step comes immediately after checking requirements in the brief's job search.

options.text: Submit the packet to the employer at once
Prepare the application packet with tailored evidence
Schedule an interview with the hiring manager
Negotiate salary and benefits with the firm

questions.explanation: After checking requirements, the candidate prepares the packet. Submitting, interviewing, and negotiating come later.

options.text: A handwritten letter in any language
A personal photo with no other details
A resume summarizing education and experience
A list of unrelated hobbies and interests

questions.explanation: Every packet needs a resume. A photo, vague letter, or hobby list cannot replace it.
questions.hint: The resume is the core document.

questions.subject: CHINESE
questions.topic: Word order when handing over documents

options.text: For review please resume accept this
Resume this please accept for your review
Accept please resume this for review
Please accept this resume for your review

questions.explanation: The natural order keeps the verb, object, and purpose clear. The distractors scramble that order.
questions.hint: Keep verb object purpose in order.

questions.explanation: Leading with relevant experience and skills signals fit. Leading with unrelated details delays the point.

stimulus.body: The brief lists three openings with different deadlines and fit levels.

questions.stem: Item 0059 asks how to prioritize in the brief.

options.text: Wait until all deadlines pass
Apply randomly to all openings
Apply only to the hardest role
Apply first to best fit with earliest deadline

questions.explanation: Prioritize best fit with earliest deadline. Random, hardest-only, or waiting misses opportunities.

questions.stem: Item 0060 asks why reviewing the packet matters in the brief.

options.text: It guarantees a job offer
It catches errors before submission
It replaces the need for tailoring
It shortens the interview

questions.explanation: Review catches errors. It does not guarantee offers, replace tailoring, or shorten interviews.
